note: Window agent p1900-p1909, 2 Nov 2026. Fills holes and leftovers the compiler leaves in 1900-1909: Lado Enclave (Congo Free State, one event and one ruling), Darfur (Ali Dinar), Tianjin and Aceh (Dutch East Indies keyframes of 1905 and 1908).

region.text: the Lado Enclave, leased to Leopold II in 1894 'for the period of his lifetime'

events.note: The Lado Enclave stayed in Congo Free State hands through the window: 'by a tacit understanding, the State was permitted to remain in occupation of the Lado Enclave' (1899), Leopold 'immediately ordered his troops to occupy the now vacant military posts' (1905), Free State commanders are listed to May 1907, and it passed to the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan only on 10 June 1910. The draft hands it to the Sudan at the founding of 1899 (size rule, 13 cells smaller) and keeps it there until 1910. This restores it to the Free State from the window's first year; the Belgian Congo then inherits it in 1908 (R2).

region.text: Darfur, Ali Dinar's sultanate: the five Darfur states, the same outline the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan dossier cuts out of its own keyframes

events.note: Darfur page: 'sultan Ali Dinar managed to re-establish Darfur's self-rule'; 'Ali Dinar's rule was recognised and tolerated by the British' until 'the British conquered Darfur in 1916'. The draft leaves 771 cells of the five Darfur states to the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan in 1900-1902 and to nobody from 1903, although the Sudan dossier's own keyframes are 'without Darfur'. They belong to the sultanate (the page restores it from 1898; applied from the window's first year).

region.text: Darfur, Ali Dinar's sultanate: the five Darfur states, the same outline the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan dossier cuts out of its own keyframes

events.note: Same sentences as events/1: Darfur was Ali Dinar's from 1898 ('re-establish Darfur's self-rule') to 1916. The draft still shows 76 cells of north Darfur as the Khedivate of Egypt's, a leftover of the Egyptian conquest of 1874 and its loss to the Mahdists ('In 1885 they conquered Darfur and destroyed Khartoum, ending Turco-Egyptian rule'), although the Khedivate's keyframe from 1899 is 'Egypt alone'.

union.text: the 1905 shape: Manchuria stays Qing land, drawn as Russian-occupied (hatched) from 1900
Tianjin and its coast, which the Qing shapes of 1900 and 1905 leave out

correction.text: the 1905 shape: Manchuria stays Qing land, drawn as Russian-occupied (hatched) from 1900; with Tianjin, which the Provisional Government of Tientsin administered from 30 July 1900 until it 'returned control of its territory to the Chinese Qing government' on 15 August 1902

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's 1905 outline has a hole of 22 cells around Tianjin that no dossier fills, so the city and its province coast are unowned in 1900-1909. The page has the city under a foreign provisional government 1900-1902 and handed back to the Qing, so it is Qing land throughout (1900-02 not hatched: no dossier for the occupiers).

union.text: Tianjin and its coast, which the Qing shapes of 1900 and 1905 leave out

keyframe_overrides.why: Same hole as qing-dynasty_1900 (the 1900 keyframe is the 1905 shape): the 1905 snap would empty the 15 Tianjin cells again. Tianjin was handed back to the Qing on 15 August 1902.

union.text: the eight cells west of 141 degrees E that the 1885 shape drops
the 1905 shape without Malaysian cells; with Karangasem (1894), Badung (1906), Luwu and Wajo (1905); with the eight edge cells west of 141 degrees E

correction.text: the 1905 shape without Malaysian cells; with Karangasem (1894), Badung (1906), Luwu and Wajo (1905); with the eight edge cells west of 141 degrees E; with Aceh, which Cliopatria draws as a separate Aceh outline until the 1914 Dutch shape

keyframe_overrides.why: Aceh War page: 'In 1904, the Sultanate of Aceh surrendered, though guerilla resistance would continue'; 'By the end of 1904, most of Aceh was under Dutch control'; the Dutch ruled it by indirect rule afterwards. The dossier's own ledger (1904 gain) gives Aceh to the Dutch East Indies, but this 1905-1907 Cliopatria shape omits Aceh, so the snap emptied 129 Aceh cells to nobody for the whole window.

The dossier's own ledger (1904 gain) gives Aceh to the Dutch East Indies, but this 1908-1913 Cliopatria shape omits Aceh, so the snap emptied 129 Aceh cells to nobody for the whole window.

rulings.why: The Anglo-Egyptian Sudan's keyframe of 1903 ('the 1899 Sudan plus the Halaib land', the 1899 Sudan being drawn 'without Darfur' and with the South Sudan) would take the enclave back from the Free State by the size rule, but the page has the Free State in occupation ('by a tacit understanding, the State was permitted to remain in occupation of the Lado Enclave', 1899), reoccupying posts in 1905, with the lease running 'for the period of his lifetime'; the Sudan took it only on 10 June 1910.
